title: Longest Listening Session
description:
Table `listen_events` records every song a user listens to on a music streaming app. It has three columns: `user_id` (INTEGER), `song_id` (INTEGER), and `listened_at` (TEXT, ISO datetime).

A **session** is a group of consecutive listens by the same user where the gap between any two adjacent listens is **30 minutes or less**. If the gap exceeds 30 minutes, a new session begins.

For each user, find their **longest session** measured by number of songs listened. Return `user_id` and `song_count` (the number of songs in their longest session).

If a user has multiple sessions tied for longest, return that count once. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
WITH gaps AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    song_id,
    listened_at,
    CASE
      WHEN (
        CAST((julianday(listened_at) - julianday(LAG(listened_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY listened_at))) * 1440 AS INTEGER) > 30
        OR LAG(listened_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY listened_at) IS NULL
      ) THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END AS new_session
  FROM listen_events
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    song_id,
    SUM(new_session) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY listened_at) AS session_id
  FROM gaps
),
session_lengths AS (
  SELECT user_id, session_id, COUNT(*) AS song_count
  FROM sessions
  GROUP BY user_id, session_id
)
SELECT user_id, MAX(song_count) AS song_count
FROM session_lengths
GROUP BY user_id;
hint: Break this into layers. First, use LAG() to find the gap in minutes between each listen and the previous one for the same user. Then flag the start of a new session when the gap exceeds 30 minutes (or it's the user's first event). Then use a running SUM() of those flags to assign a session ID. Finally, count songs per session and take the max per user.
outputExplanation: Each row represents one user and the length (in songs) of their longest listening session. A session resets whenever more than 30 minutes pass between consecutive listens.

tests.name: Exactly 31 minutes apart — splits into two sessions
Multiple users — sessions don't bleed across users
Many short sessions — longest is not the last
Tied longest sessions — return the max once
Events out of insertion order — must order by listened_at
Gap of exactly 0 minutes — same timestamp, same session
